subject.title: [Bug]: `exec` tool does not inherit `skills.entries.*.env` environment variables

question: Should credential-shaped names explicitly configured in `skills.entries.<skill>.env` bypass the generic sensitive-name block for that active skill's host run, and what isolation prevents unrelated exec leakage?
rationale: The issue is source-reproducible and contradicts documented host-run skill env behavior, but the repair intentionally moves credential values into executable subprocess environments and overlaps an open inverse secret-leak issue.

options.title: Admit scoped active-skill env secrets
options.body: Permit only keys explicitly configured for the active skill to pass the sensitive-name check, keep dangerous host/runtime names blocked, and add tests for selected-skill delivery plus unrelated exec isolation.

options.title: Keep metadata-only sensitive allowlist
options.body: Require skills to declare each sensitive env name in metadata and update docs or doctor guidance so users do not expect arbitrary credential-shaped `env` keys to work.

options.title: Defer to a new secret contract
options.body: Leave the current sanitizer unchanged until maintainers define a SecretRef or plugin-owned credential path for CLI skills that need headless auth.

recommendation.title: Admit scoped active-skill env secrets
recommendation.body: Permit only keys explicitly configured for the active skill to pass the sensitive-name check, keep dangerous host/runtime names blocked, and add tests for selected-skill delivery plus unrelated exec isolation.

likelyOwner.reason: This owner has the clearest recent merged history in the overlapping skill env lifecycle and owner-auth regression path.
